title: Whole Milk 1 gal

drivers.name: price increase (4.3%)
drivers.evidence: Past price increase to $4.34 (same as now) in 2026-03-30 (Easter) saw sales at x0.95 vs baseline; similar price rise in 2024 (Halloween) also saw x0.95. Noise-adjusted price effect is x0.95. This week has no promotion or event, so full price impact applies.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 211.0. The price is raised to $4.34 (+4.3% vs regular $4.16), a price increase with no promotion. Past data shows price increases reduce demand: the week after a promotion sees 4% below baseline, and a similar price hike in 2024 (Halloween) led to 5% below baseline. The noise-adjusted effect of price hikes is x0.95. No event or promotion is scheduled. The classical uplift model suggests no effect, but this ignores price impact. We apply a downward adjustment based on price elasticity evidence.

brief:
PRODUCT: Whole Milk 1 gal | category Dairy | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-04-20 to 2026-04-26 (next week)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 4.34 (+4.3% vs regular price 4.16)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 211.0 | 5%-95%: 166.4 - 327.6 | 10%-90%: 170.9 - 296.3

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-23% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
